To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cDNA encoding BtR-harma was cloned and expressed successfully in E.coli. BtR-har is a cadherin gene which can function as receptor for Cry1Ac.

we identified and characterized a novel cadherin-like protein from midgut of cotton bollworm, Helicoverpa amigera and demonstrated that this cadherin-like can bind Cry1Ac and is the receptor of Cry1A.
we cloned the cDNA of BtR-Harm, expressed the recombinant protein, identified the binding region of Cry1Ac, and analyzed its expression pattern and its role in resistance to Cry1Ab in H. armiger.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new cadherin gene in H. armiger and its function in Cry1Ac binding, which provides the basic data to further study on the resistance mechanisms of H. armiger to Cry1Ac.
the gene cloning, expression, and function of BtR-Harm and provides a basis for further study of the mechanism of Cry1Ac resistance in H. armi gera.

the molecular cloning and characterization of BtR- harm and its Cry1Ac binding region, which will provide the basic molecular information for the further research of BtR-armigera gene and its role in resistance of H. armigena to Cry1Ac.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cadherins of midgut in insects serve as receptors of Cry1A and are related to the resistance to Bt toxins.
cadherin is a receptor for Cry1Ac in midgut cells of H. armi-gera and the binding domain is a 244 amino acid segment.

the Cry1Ac binding region of BtR- harm was a contiguous 24 4 amino acid sequence, which may be one of the main reason for the resistance of H. armierga to Cry1Ac and the expression level of BtR-arm was related to the resistance of H.armigera to Cry1Ac.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the Cry1Ac binding domain of BtR-Harm was identified and the expression quantity of the gene significantly decreased in H. armiger resistance to Cry1C, suggesting that the Cry1C binding domain of Btharm was identified and that the expression quantity of this gene significantly decreased in the midgut of resistant H. armigere.
the BtR-harma gene is an important gene related to H. armigeras resistance to Bt toxin CrylA, which can be used as a molecular marker to identify the resistance to Cry1Ab in H. armierga.

the BtR-ham gene was cloned, the expression pattern of BtR-Ham was analyzed, the binding region of BtR- ham with Cry1Ac was determined and the expression level of BtR ham was decreased significantly in resistant strain, suggesting that BtR- Ham is the Cry1Ac receptor of H. armiger and the variation of BtR - Ham is one of the reasons for H. arniger resistance to Cry1 Ac.
